messages:
Maya: FYI — noticed a small but persistent billing spike for a handful of sessions. Looks like router truncated a streaming toolcall and the client reconnected, creating what appears to be duplicated provisional credits.
Jonathan: ugh. do we have an example session id?
Maya: sess=abc123; logs show a `TOOL_CALL_TRUNCATE` from the worker then a `RECONNECT_RESUME` that reissued the toolcall. snippet:```
INFO worker-17: session=abc123 event=TOOL_CALL_TRUNCATE offset=642
INFO router-03: session=abc123 fallback=route-b model=redwood-open-7b provisional_credits=78
INFO proxy-02: session=abc123 event=RECONNECT_RESUME offset=642 client_replay=true
```
Kevin: Are provisional credits not being deduped on reconnect? I thought we used (session_id, offset) to de-dup.
Anya: We do for normal streams, but toolcalls currently get their own provisional ledger entry keyed by `toolcall_id` only. If a truncate replaces state, toolcall_id changes when replayed.
Lee: So when truncate happens mid-toolcall we can end up with two active provisional entries: the truncated one (committed=false) and the replayed one (committed eventually). Billing UI shows both under the same time bucket -> spike.
Maya: Exactly. Billing-bot output for that session:```
billing-bot: provisional: [{id: "tlc-998", tokens: 78, committed: false}, {id: "tlc-999", tokens: 82, committed: true}]
```
Jonathan: Hmm. Two quick options: 1) tag provisional entries with `(session_id, toolcall_signature, offset_range)` so replays attach to the original provisional jam, or 2) merge in the console by showing `provisional overlaps` and smoothing spikes. Which is safer?
Kevin: Option 1 is ideal for correctness but touches the router/worker contract and may be risky mid-rollout. Option 2 is lower risk UX bandaid but delays correctness.
Anya: Implementation nuance: the router currently assigns `toolcall_signature = hash(tool_name + args)` at start. But when truncate happens we re-run the toolcall with different partial inputs and the signature legitimately changes. We could instead compute a `stable_toolcall_key = hash(session_id + tool_name + first_call_offset)` that persists across trunc+replay for same logical invocation.
Lee: That sounds good, but edgecases: what if client legitimately issues a new toolcall with same offset after user edits prompt? We might mis-merge.
Maya: True. We need a window heuristic: consider matches only within X seconds of truncate and same upstream trace id. Also make it optional behind a flag for dedicated/private accounts.
Jonathan: For the console: can we show provisional vs committed per-request, and a third column `suspected-duplicate` that groups overlapping provisional entries with a reason (e.g., `truncation/reconnect`)? That would at least make the spike explorable.
Anya: I'll prototype a ledger diff UI that groups provisional entries by overlap if they share (session_id, model, route) and have adjacent offsets. It can show: combined_tokens, candidates: [tlc-998, tlc-999], confidence: low/med/high based on trace correlation.
Kevin: Sounds good. For backend, we can add a `provisional_group_id` that is nullable. The router can attempt to link a replayed toolcall to an existing provisional_group if the heuristic matches. Group assignment can be optimistic — doesn't change committed accounting, just annotation for UI/telemetry.
Maya: Can we also emit an analytic event `provisional_group_formed` with sample size so Optimize can suggest turning on the stable-key mode for customers with frequent duplicate spikes?
Lee: Yes. That also helps product to decide rollout gating.
billing-bot: note: created provisional_group pg-47 for sess=abc123 candidates=[tlc-998,tlc-999] reason=truncate_reconnect heuristic_score=0.78
Jonathan: Timeline proposal: Anya prototypes UI grouping this week; Kevin prepares router-side flag to try `stable_toolcall_key` in canary; Maya runs a query to find top 50 affected customers and flags them with support so we can correlate.
Maya: I'll run the query and paste results here. early ask: do we want to auto-suppress provisional spikes from the default console view while we iterate?
Kevin: I'd prefer not to hide; instead surface a callout like: "Showing provisional entries; some may be duplicates due to truncation+replay — click to group". Safer.
Anya: For telemetry, emit `provisional_overlap` metric with labels: route, model, region, group_size. That will let us track prevalence.
Lee: Agree. Also add a small regression test: simulate truncate+reconnect and ensure UI groups but final committed charge equals single toolcall tokens.
Maya: Thanks folks. I'll open an ops ticket for the affected customers and label `billing:dup-provisional`. I'll also attach the log snippet and the billing-bot group id.
Jonathan: Ping me once the canary flag is ready; I'll run it on our staging replay traffic.
Maya: done. Thanks. :thumbsup:
